guide.summary: Each customer authorizes a public OAuth integration and selects pages to share. The app should request only the Read content capability, which covers reading shared page titles and content.

findings.title: Each customer authorizes through OAuth and grants page access
findings.detail: OAuth integrations act on behalf of each user, who authorizes separately and selects pages. Starting authorization requires only client credentials and a redirect URI; marketplace review is not required to begin.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers in other workspaces connect the app to read their shared pages.

evidence.quote: Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to

Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review
**Step 3** The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.

findings.title: Use a public integration so other customer workspaces can install
findings.detail: A scoped integration is limited to selected workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Making the app available to any workspace requires a public integration, and installation scope cannot be changed later.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations or workspaces will connect.

evidence.quote: ## Installation scope Choose **Or select 1 or more workspaces** when creating your integration. Only those workspaces can install it, and it cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make
your app available to any workspace, create a public integration.
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation. If you later need to make the app available to any workspace, create a new integration.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading shared pages
findings.detail: Read content gives access to read existing content. Retrieving a page or its markdown requires read content; missing capability returns 403 and access is limited to shared pages and their children.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads titles and content of pages customers explicitly share, with no create, update or administration.

findings.title: Customers must share each page through the page picker
findings.detail: Customers select pages in the page picker during authorization. The picker shows only pages the user has full access to, and sharing a parent page grants access to its children. Access applies only after the authorization flow completes.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer chooses which pages the app may read.

steps.title: Open the authorization URL and verify the callback
steps.detail: Visit the authorization URL from the Configuration tab (https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user). steps.title: Read the title of a shared page
steps.detail: Retrieve one customer-shared page. The page response may cap title mentions at 25 inline, so read the full title with the paginated property-item steps. Read title text from every result segment, not element zero, using the $.properties.*.title[].plain_text path.
steps.doneWhen: The response is 200 and the title string is returned from every title segment. Boundary check: confirm the grant is Read content only and the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the shared page.

steps.title: Read the content of a shared page as markdown
steps.detail: Retrieve the markdown of the same shared page with markdown_version=v2. Read $.markdown. If truncated is true, pass each unknown_block_id back to this endpoint as page_id and keep fetching until truncated is false or the result is object_not_found, which means inaccessible content to report explicitly. Unsupported block types such as bookmarks, embeds and link previews are not rendered; report them as unsupported rather than claiming complete content.
steps.doneWhen: The markdown string is returned; truncated subtrees are fetched or reported as inaccessible, and unsupported block types are reported. Boundary check: confirm only GET requests are sent and no write endpoint is called.

evidence.quote: Set the `markdown_version` query parameter to `v2` to get Notion-flavored Markdown instead. `v2` is recommended. `v1` is deprecated. It's the default on current Notion-Versions. See Markdown versions.
* **Truncation**: The page exceeds the record limit (approximately 20,000 blocks) and some blocks could not be loaded.
* **Unsupported block types**: Certain block types (such as bookmarks, embeds, and link previews) are not yet supported in the markdown format.

fields: markdown_version=v2: recommended Notion-flavored Markdown
PAGE_ID: same representative shared page
ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access_token from the customer's token exchange

steps.title: Fetch unknown blocks from a truncated markdown response
steps.detail: For each ID in unknown_block_ids from the previous markdown response, call the same markdown endpoint with that block ID as page_id. Repeat while truncated is true. Report object_not_found results as inaccessible, not as read content.
steps.doneWhen: Every unknown block ID is either fetched or recorded as inaccessible; no retries are attempted beyond the documented repeat.

evidence.quote: The endpoint also accepts non-navigable block IDs returned in `unknown_block_ids` from a previous truncated response. Pass these IDs to fetch additional subtrees of a large page.
When truncation or permissions cause unknown blocks, the `truncated` field is set to `true` and the `unknown_block_ids` array contains the affected block IDs.
> [!NOTE] > > The `unknown_block_ids` array does not distinguish between truncated and inaccessible blocks. Handle `object_not_found` errors gracefully when re-fetching unknown block IDs.

fields: UNKNOWN_BLOCK_ID: one value from unknown_block_ids of the prior response
